text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementArtsCan You Recognize the Subject of This Year’s Microscopic Photography Contest Winner?The Nikon Small World contest shows off objects and animals as you’ve never seen them beforeDNBy David Nield9:00 AM CDT on October 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe Nikon Small World photography contest doesn’t celebrate weather, wildlife, or natural landscapes. Instead, it’s meant to honor images of the world at the smallest possible scales, offering unique perspectives on the details of the environments around us.This year, judges cited 76 of the 1,803 entries as either an award winner, runner-up, honorable mention, or image of distinction. The contest’s mission is to “showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the microscope,” and this year’s winners definitely fulfilled that promise. There was everything from inkjet printers and pens, to wasps and neurons—all in high resolution and ultra close-up (but of course).Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
